title: Step 1: The Giant Ball
text: Imagine you are an astronaut flying high up in a spaceship. You look down from your window. What do you see? A giant, beautiful ball floating in space! It has big blue patches and green and brown spots.

title: Step 2: Think About It!
text: Where does everything we know live? Where are the oceans, mountains, animals, and your home? If we live on a ball, why don't we fall off?

content.title: Step 3: Discover Our Planet
content.description: Just like a big round football, our planet is perfectly shaped. See how the blue parts are water, and the green parts are land!

title: Step 4: This is Earth
text: The giant ball we live on is called Earth! Earth is our home. It gives us air to breathe, water to drink, and land to live on. Earth is very special because it has life.

content.preview: The planet on which we live.

content.question: What is the shape of our Earth?
What do the blue patches on the Earth stand for?

title: Step 6: Reflection Time
text: Close your eyes and think of your favorite place outside. Is it a park, a beach, or a forest? All of these beautiful places are part of our Earth. How can we keep our favorite places clean and beautiful?

title: Step 7: Connecting the Dots
text: Think about the sun that gives us light during the day, and the moon we see at night. The Earth is part of a big family in space, just like you have a family at home. We need the sun and moon just like we need the Earth!

content.title: Step 8: Earth Mastery Mission
content.description: Draw a big circle on a piece of paper. Color the water parts blue and the land parts green and brown. Draw your house on the land part to show where you live on our Earth!

content.tip: Bring a physical globe to the classroom or show a 3D model. Let the students spin it and touch the landmasses and oceans to build tactile connection.

content.mistake: Students often think the Earth is perfectly flat because the ground they walk on looks flat.
content.correction: Remind them of the ant on a huge balloon analogy. The balloon is round, but to the tiny ant, it looks flat!
